A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Global-MMLU. Their text, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved during restructuring.

before.justification: V1 reports original cultural-sensitivity annotations, translation-quality comparisons and multilingual model evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds Global-MMLU Lite evaluations, including Figure 10 and Table 4.

M1.justification: The cultural-annotation, majority-voting and translation/post-editing procedures are retained. Lite introduces evaluation sampling controls, without changing the underlying annotation method, model architecture or inference algorithm.

E1.justification: The full benchmark retains the same 42 languages, 57 MMLU subjects and multiple-choice knowledge task. Lite resamples existing annotated questions in 15 already-covered languages; it introduces no new task or domain.

E2.justification: Retained experiments use the same 14 models and the same Google Translate versus GPT-3.5-Turbo comparison. The additional Lite evaluation uses seven existing open-weight models without replacing the original comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix C introduces a substantial sampling control: Lite contains 200 CS and 200 CA questions per language, excludes 14 subjects containing only one category, matches sampling within subjects and upsamples selected categories. Its rankings reference overall Lite accuracy. Existing five-shot settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a direct test of whether CS–CA accuracy and ranking differences persist after balancing subject composition and sample counts, using Lite in Figure 10 and Table 4. V1 discussed subject-composition differences but lacked this controlled comparison.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard deviations across languages and Krippendorff’s alpha for annotation agreement. The new Lite plot follows the existing error-bar practice; no new repeated-run, seed or significance-testing procedure is disclosed.

E6.justification: V2 adds Lite accuracy results and language-specific ranking changes. Figure 10 shows higher overall CA accuracy, contrasting with the retained original evaluation’s higher CS accuracy. These are new findings under different sampling conditions, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The CS/CA definitions, majority-voting rule and metric explanations are retained. No theoretical propositions, proofs or substantive mathematical derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The introduction and conclusion add Global-MMLU Lite as a compact evaluation resource. The central claims about Western cultural bias, translation quality and changing model rankings remain, including the 28% and 84.9% headline findings.

C2.justification: V2 interprets Lite’s lower CS accuracy as evidence of difficulty associated with cultural specificity after balancing, and claims greater CS ranking volatility persists. Existing explanations and limitations are retained; the new ranking interpretation overgeneralizes Table 4.

D1.justification: Appendix C documents Lite’s exclusions, sampling quotas and upsampling. V2 adds its dataset link and permissive-license statement, plus a Qwen 2.5 source link. Existing model and annotation details are preserved through relocation.

R1.justification: The substantive related-work discussion and cited research remain unchanged. Apparent reference removals consolidate duplicate Okapi and Gemma entries, while Okapi’s publication metadata is updated.

P1.justification: The appendices are substantially reorganized from A–D into A–L. Subject taxonomy and temporal analysis move forward, and detailed model descriptions move from Section 4.1 to Appendix E. The main setup is condensed, alongside grammar, terminology and author-line edits.

P2.justification: V2 adds the Lite accuracy plot, subject-distribution plot and ranking table as Figures 10 and 13 and Table 4. Existing displays are retained, with renumbering, resizing and relocation; the overall visual format remains similar.

improvement.justification: Lite adds a useful control for the subject-composition confounding discussed in v1, together with a documented compact benchmark. However, its ranking interpretation needs correction: counting Table 4 yields 43 CA versus 33 CS rank changes, contrary to the accompanying claim of greater CS ranking volatility. The added control and resource provide a limited net improvement.
